scenes.headline: How a tiny draft model speeds up LFM2.5
scenes.sub: Liquid AI's DSpark, and why checking a block costs a sparse model more
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pebble! Liquid AI's DSpark gives three LFM2.5 models small draft models. Here's how they speed up decoding, and why the best draft gains least.

scenes.text: Decode is memory-bound. A small draft guesses a block of tokens, and the target checks them all in one pass, loading its weights once.
scenes.say: Decoding is memory-bound. So a small draft guesses a block of tokens, and the big model checks them all in one pass, loading weights once.

steps.say: A draft of about three hundred million parameters reads the target's context features, and drafts every position of a block in one pass.
Parallel drafting has no link between positions. A small sequential head adds it back, nudging each token toward what fits the one before it.

steps.note: shipped, but switched off for a fixed verify window
steps.say: A confidence head guesses which tokens will survive, so a scheduler can trim the tail. Liquid ship it, but serve a fixed window.
The target checks the whole block in one pass, keeps the prefix it agrees with, and adds its own next token. Greedy output never changes.

steps.label: Dense: nine tokens, the same weights
steps.say: A dense model reads all its weights for one token. Verifying nine tokens reads the same weights, once. The extra checks are free.

steps.label: Sparse: each token routes to its own slice
steps.say: The MoE reads about one billion of its eight billion per token. But nine tokens route to nine different slices, and the union is much larger.

scenes.title: Average speedup on the MacBook
scenes.note: the MoE's draft accepts the most: 6.95 tokens a pass
scenes.say: So on a MacBook, the MoE's draft accepts the most, six point nine five tokens a pass, and returns only one point one eight times.

scenes.text: Acceptance is a property of two models. Speedup is a property of two models and a machine.

recap: Draft a whole block in one parallel pass
A sequential head makes neighbours agree
Sparse models pay for every expert the block routes to
scenes.say: To recap: draft in parallel, verify in one pass, and mind what that pass costs a sparse model.
